root_motivation: An agent builder running two or three small services (visions/mcphost-killer-apps.md, component 4) wants an agent to know when one is down and today either pays a monitoring SaaS or polls from a machine that is itself unmonitored -- the cheapest mcphost primitives, a schedule and a table, go unused, and host.trigger.* has no worked example beyond synthetic tasks. This PRD ships a python `probe` tool that fetches a `targets` list, writes `{url, code, ms, at}` rows to a `checks` table on a 5-minute (free-plan floor) schedule, and a `status` tool that answers up/down purely from stored rows -- with zero mcphost code changes: the recipe composes host.state.*/host.tool_publish/host.trigger.* exactly as they already exist.
user_persona: Three (PRD User stories): (1) the builder's agent inserts three URLs into targets, sets the schedule, and 10 minutes later status shows two checks each; (2) the builder's agent sees one service return 503 and status shows it down with the first failing timestamp; (3) Joe's synthetic panel runs the recipe and sees how many tenants reach a stored check.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given llms.txt, When the section is read, Then it lists the two tables, two tools, and the schedule call, under 70 lines, with the calls/day arithmetic.
Given two targets and host.trigger.fire twice, When checks is queried, Then each target has exactly 2 rows with code, ms, at.
Given one target returning 503, When status is called, Then that target has up_pct_24h 0 and a down_since equal to its first check; the healthy target has 100 and no down_since.
Given a checks row older than 24h inserted by the proof, When probe runs, Then the row is gone.
Given 21 targets, When probe runs, Then it probes 20 and reports the cap in its result.
Given the proof runs against https://mcphost.dev/mcp, When it finishes, Then AC2-5 hold and wall time is printed. (Live)
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred -- operator-provisioned; Live proof against production https://mcphost.dev/mcp needs network egress and operator authorization this coding sandbox does not have. tests/mcphost_uptime_probes_ac08_live_test_skipped_without_env.rs's live_proof_against_real_mcphost_when_enabled (gated on MCPHOST_LIVE=1) is the AC6 embodiment, same convention as PRD-mcphost-team-memory's own AC6/AC8.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the synthorg task, When run 5 times, Then 5 completions record time to first stored check.
Given MCPHOST_LIVE unset, When the suite runs, Then the Live test is skipped.
Given down_since flips for a target, When probe finishes, Then one inbox message exists for the owner.

scope: www/llms.txt: new '## Uptime probes with no server' section (46 lines), appended after '## Full documentation' at end of file (so no existing section's own hardcoded NEXT_HEADING test boundary shifts) -- two host.state.table_create calls (targets, checks), two host.tool_publish calls (probe/status, kind python), the host.trigger.set(kind=schedule, schedule="*/5 * * * *") call, and the free-plan calls/day arithmetic (288 of 500).

examples/uptime-probes/tools/probe.py, status.py (new): probe.py queries targets (mcphost.state), caps at the first 20 by added_at reporting the rest as capped, fetches each with urllib (stdlib only, no pip requirement) under a 10s timeout, writes one checks row per target via mcphost.state.insert, always runs the 24h retention delete_rows, and on an up/down flip (a target assumed up with no prior history, so a target down on its very first check counts) self-calls host.msg.send over plain HTTP -- mcphost.call/composition can only reach a tenant's own published tools, never a host.* control-plane tool, so this is a real authenticated HTTP round trip using the owner's own key (published as the self_key secret) and its own endpoint (published as the ENDPOINT_URL/OWNER_NAMESPACE plain env vars), best-effort and silently skipped if either is unset. status.py reads targets/checks only (never fetches live): up_pct_24h is the 2xx share of a target's checks rows within the last 24h; down_since (present only while currently down) walks back from the newest row through the unbroken down streak to its earliest check.

examples/uptime-probes/proof.sh (new): one fresh tenant tagged x-mcphost-synthetic: recipe:uptime-probes (requirement 5); two tables, one healthy target and one that returns 503, probe published (network: public) and scheduled, host.trigger.fire twice, asserting two checks rows per target and status's up_pct_24h/down_since for both, wall time printed. Same MCP JSON-RPC curl+python3 helper shape as examples/team-memory/proof.sh.

examples/uptime-probes/synthorg-task.yaml (new): one task, segment ops_coordinator, gold.tool_name=probe / gold.kind=python / gold.call_check="result.probed == 1" -- proposed addition for RedBaron's corpus (not merged into it, same cross-repo-scope note as team-memory's own synthorg-task.yaml).

additional.zero_mcphost_code_changes: Engineering target states this explicitly: no src/**/*.rs edit is part of this PRD's scope. Every requirement is met by composing host.state.*/host.tool_publish/host.trigger.* exactly as they exist today, from python tool source and shell/docs/tests.
additional.state_not_table_store: mcphost.table (src/tables.rs, PRD-mcphost-tenant-tables) has no row-level delete -- create/append/query/list/drop/schema only, confirmed against team-memory's own forget.py tombstone workaround. AC4's 24h retention needs an actual delete, so targets/checks use mcphost.state (src/tenant_state.rs, PRD-mcphost-tenant-state) instead, whose host.state.delete_rows(table, where) does real per-row deletion under the same small filter grammar host.state.query already uses.
additional.composition_cannot_reach_host_tools: kinds::compose_call (src/kinds/mod.rs) resolves its target name through db.get_tool(tenant_id, name) -- a tenant's own published-tool row -- never a host.* control-plane tool, which dispatches through a completely different path in src/handler.rs's call_tool match. AC9's alerting hand-off therefore can't use mcphost.call("host.msg.send", ...) from inside probe.py; it self-calls the real MCP endpoint over plain HTTP instead, authenticated with the owner's own key (published as a python-kind `secrets` entry, arriving in the sandbox as SECRET_SELF_KEY per kinds::python::PythonKind::secret_env), matching how a real recipe author would have to wire this by hand.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does an agent builder running a couple of small services end up either paying a monitoring SaaS or polling from an unmonitored box?
five_whys_trace.a: mcphost's own primitives -- a schedule and a table -- are cheap enough to do this, but nothing demonstrates it: host.trigger.* has no worked example beyond synthetic tasks.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can't the builder just publish an http-kind tool that polls a URL directly?
five_whys_trace.a: http-kind has no per-tenant persistence of its own; something has to store the check history for `status` to answer 'is X up and since when' from rows, never a live fetch (Goal 2) -- that's what targets/checks (mcphost.state tables) are for.

five_whys_trace.q: Why mcphost.state (host.state.*) and not mcphost.table (host.table.*), when both already exist?
five_whys_trace.a: AC4 requires an actual delete of rows older than 24h to keep the table bounded; mcphost.table has no row-level delete (confirmed against src/tables.rs -- six ops, none of them delete), while mcphost.state's delete_rows does real per-row deletion under its own filter grammar.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the P2 alerting hand-off (AC9) need a raw HTTP self-call instead of just calling host.msg.send from inside probe.py?
five_whys_trace.a: kinds::compose_call only resolves a tenant's own published tools (db.get_tool), never a host.* control-plane tool -- confirmed against src/kinds/mod.rs's compose_call and src/handler.rs's call_tool dispatch, which route host.* calls through an entirely separate arm. The only way probe.py can reach host.msg.send is the same way an external client would: an authenticated HTTP POST to the endpoint itself.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is a synthorg task part of this PRD rather than left to a follow-on?
five_whys_trace.a: The PRD's own secondary success metric is 'time to first stored check (synthetic, using trigger.fire), p50 under 90s, synthorg ledger, first 20 runs' -- that claim is only real once something actually times it, the same reasoning every prior recipe PRD in this repo (team-memory, share-a-tool) already established as this repo's convention for a landed recipe.
